title: Interfaces and Type Aliases
summary: Naming object shapes, optional and readonly members, extending, and structural typing.

steps.title: Naming a shape
body: Two ways to name an object type:
```ts
interface User {
id: number;
name: string;
email?: string;            // optional: string | undefined
readonly createdAt: string; // cannot be assigned after creation
type Point = { x: number; y: number };
**Structural typing:** unlike C#, a value matches an interface if it has the right **shape**. It never has to say `implements`:
```ts
const u = { id: 1, name: "Ada", createdAt: "2024-01-01" };
function greet(user: User) { return user.name; }
greet(u);                    // fine: u has the shape
One catch: an object literal written **directly** where a type is expected may not have extra properties (`greet({ id: 1, name: "A", createdAt: "", age: 3 })` is an error, to catch typos).

steps.explain: Structural typing: shape, not declared name, decides. The extra `age` is fine because `p` is a variable, not a fresh literal.

steps.title: interface or type?
body: They overlap heavily. The differences that matter:
| | `interface` | `type` |
| object shapes | yes | yes |
| unions, tuples, primitives, function types | no | yes: `type Id = string \| number` |
| extend | `interface Admin extends User { level: number }` | `type Admin = User & { level: number }` |
| reopen later to add members | yes (declaration merging) | no |
| `class X implements ...` | yes | yes (object types) |
A common rule: `interface` for object shapes and public APIs, `type` for unions and everything else. React component props are written either way; be consistent.

steps.title: readonly
body: `readonly` makes assignment a compile error. It is the TypeScript side of the immutability habit from module 3:
```ts
interface Config { readonly apiUrl: string }
const c: Config = { apiUrl: "/api" };
c.apiUrl = "/v2";                    // error: Cannot assign to 'apiUrl' because it is a read-only property.
function sum(xs: readonly number[]) {
xs.push(1);                        // error: Property 'push' does not exist on type 'readonly number[]'.
return xs.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0);
const ROUTES = ["/", "/about"] as const;   // readonly ["/", "/about"]: literal types, frozen
Like `Object.freeze`, it is shallow, and unlike `freeze`, it does nothing at run time.

steps.title: Model a product
prompt: and an `interface DigitalProduct extends Product` that adds `downloadUrl: string`.
Then write `label(p: Product): string` returning `"<name> ($<price>)"` followed by ` [tag1, tag2]` when there are tags.
label({ id: 2, name: "Font", priceCents: 500, tags: ["ttf", "web"] }) // "Font ($5.00) [ttf, web]"
template: Dojo.eq("no tags", "Mug ($12.00)", label({ id: 1, name: "Mug", priceCents: 1200 }));
Dojo.eq("with tags", "Font ($5.00) [ttf, web]", label({ id: 2, name: "Font", priceCents: 500, tags: ["ttf", "web"] }));
Dojo.eq("empty tags", "Pen ($1.50)", label({ id: 3, name: "Pen", priceCents: 150, tags: [] }));
const dojoD: DigitalProduct = { id: 4, name: "Ebook", priceCents: 999, downloadUrl: "/dl/4" };
Dojo.eq("a DigitalProduct is a Product", "Ebook ($9.99)", label(dojoD));
hints: `tags?: string[]` is optional; `p.tags?.length` is `undefined` when missing.
